_meta.purpose: Sweep totals for 2026-09-25T07:30:02Z, written by export-site-data.py on the machine.
_meta.contents: 45 boards read, 3837 postings observed on those boards, 83 postings reached a verdict, 80 verified live, 3 killed, 3 of those caught by a named rule. Every count reconciles against the files beside it.
_meta.pulled_means: pulled is 83, which is verified plus killed, and it counts the postings that passed the title and location filters and therefore reached a verdict. It is not the 3837 postings read off the boards: the site's own contract requires verified plus killed to equal pulled, so this field has to be the set that got a verdict. The board total is postings_observed below.
_meta.boards_that_failed_note: A board that answered with an empty list is not in this list. It is a company that is not hiring, which is a fact rather than a failure.
_meta.no_sweep_number: There is no sweep_number and there will not be one. It was derived by counting run records in the archive, which meant a test run incremented it, a re-read of the archive changed it, and two machines disagreed about it. swept_at_utc is the identifier: it cannot be incremented by accident and it is already what the site's footer publishes. Dropped 2026-08-19.
_meta.killed_by_rule: One key per live rule, always all of them, always including the zeroes. A rule missing from this object reads as a rule that was never run, and several of these are expected to sit at zero for weeks. killed_unattributed is 0: kills carrying no rule the site still publishes, which today means records the retired evergreen rule produced.
_meta.clock: One clock. Every instant here and in jobs.json is this sweep's, in UTC, to the second.
